input.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
input.rationale: Paragraph 4(a) is the only convenience-termination mechanic in the Agreement. Three fallback elements already sit in the text: the mutual right to terminate for any reason after the Initial Term "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party" gives AP a 90-day exit and simultaneously obliges Kubient to give AP 90 days' notice; and the only termination-linked payment is fees generated during that termination period, i.e. ordinary revenue earned through the notice period and no more than three months' fees. The clause fails the fallback on one material term: Kubient's right is untethered to term-end, so it may exit for convenience mid-renewal-term (an auto-renewal/notice right is not term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly anchored to the end of the then-current term). Our single edit appends a proviso confining any Kubient termination to the end of the then-current Term, leaving the mutual 90-day notice, the Initial Term lock, the breach/insolvency rights and the fee sentence verbatim. We do not pursue the preferred position (30 days' notice and pro-rata refund of prepaid fees), which is a poor fit for this revenue-share structure with no prepaid fees.

proposal.summary: Keep the mutual 90-day convenience notice but confine Kubient's termination to the end of the then-current Term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have kept the mutual 90 days' written notice requirement intact and added a proviso that any termination by Kubient takes effect only at the end of the then-current Term, so AP can exit on notice while Kubient cannot walk away mid-term. This is our fallback position.
